Pacino Docs · Open Source 8-issue OOO RISC-V Processor CORE AI co-designed I-CACHE D-CACHE MEM CTRL I/O I/O uarchlabs.github.io/pacino open source · 2026 // overview "I'm out of order? You're out of order!"

Pacino is an open source 8-issue out-of-order RISC-V processor targeting the RVA23S64 profile. RTL is written in SystemVerilog, simulated with Verilator, and verified with a combination of directed tests, functional coverage, formal analysis via SymbiYosys and riscv-formal, and spike-dasm as an independent oracle. Gate synthesis targets Yosys with FPGA mapping via Quartus and Vivado. Design decisions, AI-assisted co-design records, and architectural rationale are committed alongside the RTL.

Pacino is designed using a structured AI co-design methodology — a domain expert directing a dual-agent workflow across architectural planning and RTL implementation. Prompts, iteration history, and design rationale are committed alongside the RTL as first-class artifacts. Full methodology documentation is in the FAQ and the repo.

docs.title: IA task browser
docs.text:
Anatomy of a task file

Written before the run, by the designer and the PA:

  • Header: task ID, date, module, model, runtime, context used, PA session, task type, mode and status
  • Overview: a short summary
  • Context: the files the IA loads, kept deliberately small
  • Hypothesis: the question the task is asking
  • Background: what the IA, or a human reader, needs to know
  • Binding previous decisions: earlier decisions that apply, which the IA can use to check that the task makes sense
  • Requirements: what the run must deliver
  • Constraints: the limits of the run

Written by the IA, in Results Capture:

  • What was delivered, the test matrix and the test results
  • Assumptions and decisions the IA made where the prompt gave no guidance
  • RVA23 compliance risks and edge behavior
  • Deferred work and other notes
  • Files modified, and a context usage report

Written after the run, in the results discussion: the IA's console output, my assessment and the PA's assessment.

docs.title: Frontend Overview
docs.text:
Pacino implements a 'decoupled frontend' with a branch prediction cluster of 7 predictors feeding an instruction fetch unit, an address translation stage and an instruction decoder which can decode at least 8 instructions per cycle.

This page is an introduction to Pacino's frontend. The discussion walks through the two diagrams below covering the operation of the frontend and coordination between the components.

The design decisions which arrived at this implementation are found in the planning documents pacino/planning/arch. These are linked at the end.

There are waveform views of the principal operations of the frontend. Major behaviors are described here: frontend demonstration.

These pages aim to be readable by newer designers without being tedious for experienced ones; feedback on the level of detail is welcome.

Experienced designers may prefer to go directly to the specs and RTL.

docs.title: A decoupled frontend
docs.text:
In baseline frontends branch prediction and instruction fetch operate in lockstep. The predictor chooses the next address, the instruction cache reads it, and the next prediction waits for the fetch to finish.

Performance of this basic microarchitecture is improved by decoupling portions of the frontend. Pacino implements a decoupled frontend based on a fetch target queue (FTQ).

The branch predictor produces a stream of predicted fetch addresses and writes these to the FTQ. The fetch unit (IFU) processes entries in the FTQ in order as they appear. This weakens the interlock between prediction and fetch/icache access. This organization was introduced by Reinman, Austin and Calder [1].

The FTQ serves another purpose: it provides a look ahead of addresses that fetch will need soon, telling the processor which instruction cache lines to bring in. This mechanism is the basis for fetch-directed prefetching [2]. Pacino's future prefetch mechanism will use this mechanism.

Because an FTQ entry can be corrected after it is written, the FTQ lets a fast, simple predictor start fetch immediately while slower, more accurate predictors perform their look ups. When the slower predictors agree with the fast predictor, cycles of latency are saved [3].

Decoupled frontends of this kind are now standard in high-performance cores; these can be found in public information on commercial designs [4]. The XiangShan series of open source designs also implement decoupled frontends [5].

FTQ management logic uses the state in each entry to assist branch predictor training and to restore processor state on mispredictions. Pacino uses a redirect mechanism so that early start predictions can be corrected when the slower more accurate predictor(s) disagree. A redirect will find and discard every younger entry and each associated in-flight fetch.

Prediction can run ahead only as far as the branch target buffer (BTB) can identify branch locations. On a BTB miss, the branch is not identified, the direction and target predictors are never consulted and the block is predicted to fall through to a default, the ‘fall-through address’. If that branch is taken, the predicted stream, and any prefetching driven by it, continues down the fall-through path until predecode or branch resolution in the backend detects the branch and redirects fetch. Much recent work addresses this limit [6, 7].

docs.title: The two views
docs.text:
The Pacino frontend (FE) is one structural module, fe_top. There are seven sub-modules:

Blk Description BPC branch prediction cluster FTQ fetch target queue IFU instruction fetch unit ITLB instruction translation lookaside buffer L1I level 1 instruction cache IBUF instruction buffer decode instruction decoder

There are two views of the FE.

The block view shows these units and the interfaces. The annotations on the signals refer to sections of the connectivity inventory, which lists each signal.

The pipeline view shows the same units aligned to pipeline stages.

Both diagrams show a Pacino FE configured for dual prediction; the demonstration's default build uses one slot.

Select either diagram to open it at full size.

docs.title: Pacino’s three pipelines
docs.text:
The frontend is built as three pipelines that run independently:

  1. The prediction pipeline, in the branch prediction cluster (bp_cluster), decides which code comes next.
  2. The translation pipeline, in the instruction fetch unit (IFU) and the instruction TLB, turns each predicted address into a physical address.
  3. The fetch pipeline, in the IFU and the level-one instruction cache (L1I), reads the bytes, finds the instructions in them and passes them on to the instruction buffer and decode.

In Pacino the branch prediction cluster writes predicted blocks into a 64-entry FTQ, and the IFU takes them from the FTQ in order.

The FTQ speculatively uses the prediction available in p1, formed by the micro-BTB (uBTB) and the loop predictor (LP), to allocate the entry and begin fetch. If later predictions disagree, e.g. in p2 or p3 from TAGE or SC, the FTQ entry is corrected and a redirect occurs. Redirects cancel any incorrect pending fetches and start fetches from the corrected (redirected) address.

Pacino also decouples address translation: the instruction TLB works on the FTQ through its own pointer, xlate_ptr, ahead of fetch, so a translation can complete before fetch reaches the block.

This arrangement is the core of Pacino's decoupled frontend. Prediction can run ahead of fetch while fetch is waiting, for example on a cache miss, so the FTQ fills with the addresses fetch will need next. The pipeline view shows this: its two halves are not aligned in time, because they are linked only through the queue.

The FTQ tracks its entries with four pointers, oldest first: commit_ptr (entries the backend has retired), fetch_ptr (the next entry to fetch), xlate_ptr (the next entry to translate) and alloc_ptr (the next entry the prediction pipeline will write).

docs.title: Prediction blocks and slots
docs.text:
In Pacino the unit of prediction is the prediction block: up to 32 bytes of code that begin at any 2-byte address. A block ends at the first branch predicted taken, and the next block begins at that branch's target. One FTQ entry holds one prediction block.

A block can contain more than one branch. Each prediction slot describes one of them, and the compile time parameter NUM_PRED_SLOTS sets how many slots a block has. With two slots, the frontend can predict two branches in one block, so a not-taken branch does not end the block early. When a block holds more branches than it has slots, the block ends at the first branch it cannot describe, and the next block starts with that branch.

The prediction block is not the same as the 64-byte cache line the IFU reads from the L1I. The IFU reads a whole line and extracts the block from it.

docs.title: The prediction pipeline
docs.text:
Prediction takes up to four cycles, p0 to p3. Each stage has its own predictors, and each later stage may correct the earlier answer.

Stage Operation Predictors p0 The FTQ presents the block's start address. Table indices are formed from the address and the branch history. RAS top-of-stack read p1 The initial prediction is formed. The FTQ allocates an entry and fetch can begin. uBTB, loop predictor p2 The block's contents and the main direction and target predictions arrive. FTB, TAGE, ITTAGE, RAS push or pop, loop predictor re-read p3 The statistical corrector gives the final direction. SC

The FTQ never waits for a predictor later than p1. A later stage that disagrees with what the FTQ already holds sends a redirect instead, which rewrites the entry and restarts fetch from the corrected address.

The seven predictors, and the module that keeps the branch history, are:

  • uBTB (micro branch target buffer, 256 entries, 4-way). A small, combinational predictor that gives the first guess at p1.
  • Loop predictor. Learns the trip count of regular loops so that the loop's exit is predicted correctly. It answers at p1 and again at p2.
  • FTB (fetch target buffer, 2048 entries, 4-way). Records, for each block start address, where the block ends and the branches in it: their positions, types and targets. It is the authority on what a block contains.
  • TAGE. The main direction predictor for conditional branches: a base table T0 and four tagged tables, T1 to T4, each of 2048 entries. The tagged tables are indexed by the address combined with 8, 13, 32 and 119 bits of branch history.
  • SC (statistical corrector). Can reverse TAGE's direction at p3 when its own counters disagree strongly.
  • ITTAGE. Predicts the targets of indirect jumps, built like TAGE but storing targets instead of directions.
  • RAS (return address stack). Predicts return addresses. Calls push it and returns pop it.
  • History module (bp_history). Keeps the global branch history (256 bits) that the history-indexed predictors use, and checkpoints it so that it can be restored after a misprediction.

At p2 the FTB will know the branch type. The type decides which predictor supplies the target:

Branch type Target comes from Return RAS Indirect jump ITTAGE Conditional branch The FTB's target if taken, otherwise the next block Direct jump FTB

For conditional branches without a trusted loop prediction, the later-stage predictors are assumed to be more accurate. In order of precedence: SC, TAGE, the FTB, then the uBTB. TAGE and the FTB outputs are valid at p2; TAGE takes precedence over the FTB.

A trusted loop prediction outranks all of these. Once the loop predictor is confident in a loop’s trip count, its p2 direction stands. In this case the SC does not override it at p3.

docs.title: Redirects
docs.text:
Three places can redirect fetch:

  1. The prediction pipeline at p2 or p3, when a later predictor corrects the initial prediction.
  2. Predecode, in the IFU, when the bytes fetched contradict the prediction, for example a branch where the prediction assumed none.
  3. The backend, when a branch resolves differently from its prediction.

A redirect names one FTQ entry and one slot. A later stage wins over an earlier stage for the same entry and slot. The younger blocks already in flight are dropped from both IFU pipelines, and fetch restarts from the new address.

The time from a redirect to the first translation request at the new address is short:

Redirect source Cycles to the new translation request p2 or p3 prediction 1 Predecode 2 Backend 2

A backend redirect also clears the IBUF. Prediction redirects do not.

docs.title: Translation and fetch
docs.text:
The translation pipeline takes the entry at xlate_ptr. The ITLB (64 entries, includes PMP and PMA checks) translates the block's start address in one cycle on a hit. A block that crosses a page boundary requires a second lookup in the next cycle. A miss goes to the page table walker (PTW). The resulting physical address with memory attributes or a fault waits in a four-entry queue for fetch.

The fetch pipeline takes the entry at fetch_ptr and runs in four stages:

Stage What happens F0 Accept the request, read the translation, and send zero to two requests to the L1I. F1 Compute the address of every 2-byte position in the block while the cache access is in flight. F2 The cache line returns. Check for faults and select the 17 halfwords that hold the block. (32 bytes, plus 2 for a 32-bit instruction that starts in the last halfword) F3 Expand compressed instructions, predecode, check the prediction, and write the instructions to the instruction buffer.

After F3, a writeback stage reports what predecode found back to the FTQ. This is where the frontend learns, from the bytes themselves, whether the prediction described the block correctly.

The L1I is 64 KiB, 8-way set associative, with 64-byte lines, and returns data two cycles after a request on a hit.

docs.title: Instruction buffer and decode
docs.text:
The instruction buffer (IBUF, 64 entries) accepts up to 16 instructions per cycle from F3 and releases up to 8 from its head. When it is empty, F3's writes pass straight through to the read port.

Decode is eight instructions wide and combinational. It decodes the RVA23 scalar and vector encodings into the internal format the backend consumes.

docs.title: Branch Predictor Training
docs.text:
When the backend resolves a branch, it reports the outcome to the FTQ. The FTQ reads the prediction-time metadata stored with the branch's FTQ entry. This metadata is generated and returned by each predictor with the prediction. The FTQ forms an update for each involved predictor based on branch type:

Branch type Predictors updated Conditional uBTB, loop predictor, FTB, TAGE, SC Indirect uBTB, FTB, ITTAGE Return uBTB, FTB, RAS Direct jump uBTB, FTB Call uBTB, FTB, RAS; an indirect call also ITTAGE

Updates are sent as soon as a branch resolves rather than at retire. TAGE, SC and ITTAGE take updates through a queue in front of their tables, and an update takes two stages, u0 and u1, with single cycle throughput.

A prediction can read a table entry before a pending update to it has been written. That costs some prediction accuracy; in exchange, a prediction is never delayed. The table arbiters always grant predictions first, and an update writes only in a cycle with no prediction presented.

docs.title: The FE Boundary
docs.text:
Three groups of signals cross the fe_top boundary:

  • Backend. Decoded instructions are sent to rename. Branch resolutions, redirects and commits come back to the FTQ, and FENCE.I and cbo.inval come from the commit stage to the IFU.
  • Translation. The instruction TLB's path to the page table walker.
  • Memory. The L1I’s port to the level-two cache.

Some control inputs come from units not yet built: the CSR state, the predictor configuration and the TLB invalidate. The testbenches drive them, and they are the “in:” labels in the block view. The dashed boxes are the testbench models of the backend, the page table walker and memory.

docs.title: BP Cluster Micro-Architectural Decisions
docs.text:
FILE:    bp_cluster.md
 SOURCE:  various
 STATUS:  DRAFT
 UPDATED: 2026-10-08
 CONTACT: Jeff Nye

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
8-issue OoO RISC-V RVA23 branch predictor cluster. Optionally dual prediction (Xiangshan model): two predictions per 32-byte block, one per prediction slot. THE SLOTS ARE THE BLOCK'S TWO BRANCH FIELDS, br0 and br1, NOT TWO NEXT-PC SLOTS: one lookup supplies both, and a taken branch ends the block (fe_decisions.md 10, FE-10, FE-11). See Dual Prediction Mode below. Dual mode is runtime-selectable via a static configuration input. An earlier revision read "two independent next-PC predictions per fetch bundle"; corrected session-070.

Predictors: uBTB, Loop, FTB, TAGE, SC, ITTAGE, RAS.

Override order (conditional branch direction and target):
  uBTB (p1) -> FTB, TAGE (p2) -> SC (p3)
  ON DIRECTION this IS a ranking: SC > TAGE > FTB, all three produce
  that one quantity, with a trusted loop prediction above all three
  since BP-122 (fe_decisions.md 3.3), suspended per branch when the
  FTB fast path
  fires (ftb_confidence_override_rules.md 4.3, 4.2). ON EVERYTHING
  ELSE it is stage order, not a ranking: a later stage supersedes an
  earlier one (FE-3, fe_decisions.md 12, narrowed session-070), and
  targets are selected by branch type.
  Loop predictor overrides uBTB at p1 when trusted, that is when
  lp_pred_is_loop is set (Loop Predictor above). Since BP-122 its p2
  re-read is also the slot's direction at p2 and p3 when trusted.
  This read "Loop predictor does not participate after p1".
  ITTAGE and RAS are outside this ordering (type-gated, see below).

docs.title: Block width
docs.text:
The successor on a uBTB miss is PC + FTB_BLOCK_BYTES, 32 bytes.

FTB_BLOCK_BYTES is 32, the PREDICTION block. FETCH_BLOCK_BYTES is 64, the FETCH block, a global parameter: the L1I line the IFU reads (fe_decisions.md Conventions). ftb_decisions.md 2.3 rules that the two are independent and must not be collapsed: treating the 64-byte fetch as a 64-byte prediction reintroduces a two-block-per-cycle structure and would demand four conditional-branch predictions per cycle against a two-prediction budget.

AN EARLIER REVISION OF THIS DOCUMENT wrote the miss successor as PC + fetch_width at both sites below. fetch_width here is FETCH_BLOCK_BYTES, 64, so the successor skipped a whole prediction block: the 32 bytes between PC+32 and PC+64 went unpredicted and a branch in them was missed until the p2 redirect corrected it. Bounded to one cycle, but a wrong successor is written into the FTQ entry in the meantime. Corrected session-069.

The base is the lookup PC, not the aligned address containing it. Prediction blocks are unaligned (ftq_decisions.md 4.7, ifu_decisions.md IFU-6), and a miss does not resync the stream to a 32-byte boundary.

BUILT by BP-110 (TD#125, closed): bp_cluster.sv no longer forms any in-block address from the aligned base, the miss successor is lookup PC + 32, and the branch PC is block START + (pos << POS_OFFSET_BITS) (ftb_decisions.md 4.6 R-2). This read "AS BUILT, bp_cluster.sv forms both the miss successor and the branch PC from the 32-byte-ALIGNED base", from the session-071 RTL read; stale since BP-110. Session-076.

docs.title: uBTB (micro Branch Target Buffer)
docs.text:
- Size:    256 entries, 4-way associative
- Stage:   p1 output
- Role:    First prediction. Provides next-PC to start speculative fetch.
           On miss: no prediction generated. Fetch proceeds
           sequentially (PC + FTB_BLOCK_BYTES, 32 bytes) until the
           p2 redirect fires. The base is the LOOKUP PC, not the
           32-byte-aligned address containing it, so a miss does
           not resync the stream to alignment.
           uBTB does not generate a redirect signal. It supplies or
           withholds an initial prediction only.

docs.title: Loop Predictor
docs.text:
- Size:    256 entries, 4-way associative
           LP_N_SETS = LP_TBL_ENTRIES / LP_TBL_WAYS = 64 sets
           LP_IDX_BITS = $clog2(64) = 6b
- Stage:   p1 output (same timing as uBTB)
- Role:    Detects loop branches and predicts exit. Overrides uBTB at
           p1 when loop predictor is trusted. THE TRUST TEST IS
           INSIDE loop_pred: lp_pred_is_loop is set only on a hit
           with cnf == LP_CONF_LEVEL (loop_pred_interfaces.md
           Semantics). The cluster's p1 mux then selects on
           lp_pred_is_loop alone. This read "Trust decision made by
           override control, not internally". Session-072.
- Parameters (all overridable at elaboration):
    LP_TBL_ENTRIES = 256
    LP_TBL_WAYS    = 4
    LP_TAG_BITS    = 14
    LP_ITR_BITS    = 14   -- iteration counter width
    LP_CNF_BITS    = 2    -- confidence counter width
    LP_AGE_BITS    = 8    -- age/replacement counter width
    LP_N_SETS      = LP_TBL_ENTRIES / LP_TBL_WAYS
    LP_IDX_BITS    = $clog2(LP_N_SETS), min 1
- Override: sits alongside uBTB in p1. The p1 mux selects the loop
           predictor's DIRECTION over the uBTB's when
           lp_pred_is_loop is set; the target comes from the uBTB
           entry (ftq_bpu_interfaces.md 4). Does not participate in
           the p2/p3 override chain.
- Status:  BUILT by BP-122 (TD#169): read before write, the
           speculative count advanced at p2 with a per-FTQ-entry
           checkpoint, and a trusted p2 direction over TAGE and SC.
           Used in lp and loops. loop_pred_interfaces.md.

docs.title: FTB (Fetch Target Buffer, aka BTB)
docs.text:
- Size:    2048 entries, 4-way associative, 512 sets
           FTB_WAYS = 4, FTB_ENTRIES = 2048, FTB_SETS = 512.
           `ftb_decisions.md` 2.2 and section 8 are the reference;
           do not restate the geometry here.
- Stage:   p2 output (p0 send, p1 registered, p2 valid)
- Role:    Authoritative branch target for direct conditional and
           unconditional branches. Identifies branch type per slot,
           gating which predictor provides the target at p2:
             return     -> RAS provides target
             indirect   -> ITTAGE provides target
             conditional -> TAGE provides direction, FTB provides target
             direct unc -> FTB provides target

docs.title: TAGE
docs.text:
- Stage:   p2 output (p0 index calc, p1 SRAM read + tag match, p2 final)
- Role:    Direction prediction for conditional branches. OVERRIDES
           THE FTB DIRECTION: the FTB submits its own direction for
           every valid conditional (conf MSB on ftb_brI_taken_p2)
           and TAGE supersedes it at p2. fe_decisions.md 3.3;
           ftb_confidence_override_rules.md 3.1, 4.3 and 8, where
           the direction priority is SC > TAGE > FTB.
           EXCEPT UNDER THE FAST PATH: when ftb_fastpath_p2[i]
           fires -- conf saturated and ftb_fastpath_en set -- the
           FTB direction stands for that branch and no TAGE or SC
           direction override is applied. TAGE and SC are still
           requested and still trained
           (ftb_confidence_override_rules.md 4.2, 6).
           THE REDIRECT IS A SEPARATE QUESTION. p2_redirect fires
           only when the successor the cluster would publish differs
           from the one its own p1 stage registers hold, not on the
           override itself: an override that does not change the
           successor fires nothing (fe_decisions.md FE-4, 2.5).
           An earlier revision read "p2_redirect fires on override";
           a session-070 revision then over-corrected and denied the
           direction override itself. Both corrected session-070.
- Tables:
    T0: 2 ways x 2048 entries, base table
        Entry layout: 2b CTR (no tag, no valid, no useful)
    T1: 2 banks x 2048, FH=8b,  FH1=8b,  FH2=7b,  hist=8b
    T2: 2 banks x 2048, FH=11b, FH1=8b,  FH2=7b,  hist=13b
    T3: 2 banks x 2048, FH=11b, FH1=8b,  FH2=7b,  hist=32b
    T4: 2 banks x 2048, FH=11b, FH1=8b,  FH2=7b,  hist=119b
    T1-T4 tagged entry: TAG EPC USE CTR VALID, MSB to LSB. The
        field order and widths are owned by
        tage_table_entry_formats.md; by default tag 8b, epc 2b,
        useful 2b, ctr 3b, valid 1b. This listed valid, tag, ctr
        and useful with no EPC. Session-072.

docs.title: SC (Statistical Corrector)
docs.text:
- Stage:   p3 output. The SC path STARTS AT p2, not p0: the TAGE p2
           result and the p0 inputs staged forward are presented at
           p2, the table index hashes are computed at p2, the table
           RAM reads issue at p2, and the result is valid at p3. The
           update path is u0/u1. sc_decisions.md 2 and 9,
           sc_interfaces.md Timing, sc_table_interfaces.md Table
           Pipeline, bp_arb_spec.md 6.1. An earlier revision read
           "p0 index, p1 counter read, p2 accumulate, p3 final",
           which is a four-stage path this design does not have.
           Corrected session-070.
- Role:    Corrects TAGE when TAGE is systematically biased. Requires
           TAGE output to proceed (TAGE must be valid before SC can
           finalize). Overrides TAGE direction when combined counter
           magnitude exceeds threshold, subject to the FTB fast
           path (ftb_confidence_override_rules.md 4.2). The p3
           redirect fires only when SC CHANGES WHAT THE CLUSTER
           PUBLISHED AT p2, not on the override itself
           (fe_decisions.md 3.1, FE-4). An earlier revision read
           "p3_redirect fires on override"; corrected session-070.
           Threshold: dynamically adapted at runtime (O-GEHL scheme,
           TC counter), not a fixed design-time value and not CSR-
           configurable. See sc_decisions.md sections 9-10, G7.
- Arbitration: the SC arbiter is in bp_cluster. Since BP-121 a
           prediction is never delayed and an SC update is granted
           only with no block at p2 that TAGE answers
           (bp_arb_spec.md 4.5). The SC request is formed for every
           block TAGE answers at p2, squashed or not (r_tv_p2,
           BP-121 D13).

- Tables:
    ST0: 512 entries, direct mapped, 6b wide, hist=0b
         No folded history (hist=0).
    ST1: 512 entries, direct mapped, 6b wide, hist=4b
    ST2: 512 entries, direct mapped, 6b wide, hist=16b
    ST3: 512 entries, direct mapped, 6b wide, hist=64b
    ST4: 1024 entries, direct mapped, 6b wide, hist=none
         No folded history (BrIMLI index, not a hashed fold).

docs.title: ITTAGE (Indirect Target TAGE)
docs.text:
- Stage:   p2 output (p0 index and tag hash, p1 SRAM read + tag
           match, p2 final target)
- Role:    Target prediction for indirect non-return branches (JALR
           non-return). Target stored directly in the ITTAGE tables --
           no base+offset secondary LUT. Active only when FTB
           identifies branch type as indirect.
- Target:  40b, VA[40:1]. Bit 0 is always zero for instruction
           alignment and is not stored. IT_MAX_TGT_WIDTH = 40 and the
           reconstruction is {stored, 1'b0}; no target bit is
           inferred by extension. Built by BP-111 (TD#132, closed).
           This read "38b ... must zero-extend; TD#122", stale since
           BP-111. Session-076. See ittage_interfaces.md.
- Tables:
    IT1: 2 banks x 256 entries, FH=4b,  FH1=4b,  FH2=4b,  hist=4b
    IT2: 2 banks x 256 entries, FH=8b,  FH1=8b,  FH2=8b,  hist=8b
    IT3: 2 banks x 512 entries, FH=9b,  FH1=9b,  FH2=8b,  hist=13b
    IT4: 2 banks x 512 entries, FH=9b,  FH1=9b,  FH2=8b,  hist=16b
    IT5: 2 banks x 512 entries, FH=9b, FH1=9b, FH2=8b, hist=32b

docs.title: RAS (Return Address Stack)
docs.text:
Dual-stack, static partition: 16 speculative + 32 commit entries, pointer-only snapshot recovery. Push and pop at p2, type-gated on the FTB branch type; p3 applies an inverse repair when the p3 view, qualified by p3 reachability, disagrees with p2 (BP-121, TD#166). The pushed return address is the call PC plus 2 or 4 from the FTB jump field's rvc bit (BP-121, TD#164). Outside the conditional override chain: RAS supplies the target for a return, ITTAGE for every other indirect JALR, and the FTB target is the ITTAGE-miss fallback, not a third arm.

ras_decisions.md is the one home for all of it: role and repair table 1, call and return detection with the full JALR hint table 2, the stacks and pointers 3, snapshot and restore 4, the recursion counter 5, dual-slot behaviour 6, return address value 8, parameters 9.

This section restated the whole of that -- structure, pointers, pipeline, the repair table, the hint table and the JALR roles -- under a session-050 decision recording the duplication as intentional. PROJECT_CORE.md places each rule in exactly one document, and this file already says so of 4.3 and 4.4 (Update Policy). The hint table, which ras_decisions.md 2 pointed here for, moved there. Session-071.

docs.title: Pipeline Staging
docs.text:
Cycle N   (p0): PC input. Index calculations begin in the
                  predictors that index at p0.
                  FTB, TAGE, ITTAGE send address to SRAM.
                  SC DOES NOT. Its path starts at p2; see the SC
                  Stage bullet. An earlier revision listed SC here
                  and at p1; corrected session-070.

  Cycle N+1 (p1): uBTB output valid -> first prediction available.
                  Loop predictor output valid -> overrides uBTB if
                  lp_pred_is_loop is set.
                  Fetch begins speculatively on p1 result.
                  On uBTB miss and lp_pred_is_loop clear: fetch
                  proceeds PC + FTB_BLOCK_BYTES.
                  TAGE: SRAM read completes, tag match, slot reorder.
                  FTB: result registered (arrives too late for p1).
                  SC: nothing. It has not started.

  Cycle N+2 (p2): FTB output valid (registered from p1).
                  TAGE final result valid.
                  RAS: push/pop executes, ras_pop_addr_p2 valid.
                  ITTAGE: final target valid.
                  SC STARTS HERE: the TAGE p2 result and the staged
                      p0 inputs are presented, index hashes are
                      computed, and the table RAM reads issue. Result
                      at p3. sc_decisions.md 2 and 9,
                      sc_table_interfaces.md Table Pipeline.
                  p2_redirect fires if the successor the cluster
                  would publish at p2, formed from FTB/TAGE/RAS/ITTAGE,
                  differs from its own p1 stage registers (FE-4).
                  FTB entry saved for one additional cycle (-> p3).

  Cycle N+3 (p3): SC final result valid -> p3_redirect if the p3
                  successor differs from the cluster's own p2 stage
                  registers (FE-4). This read "if SC != p2",
                  predictor against stage. Session-071.
                  RAS p3 = p2 registered. Stack repair if p3 != p2.
                  FTB entry from p2 held and available.

docs.title: Redirect Architecture
docs.text:
Two redirect points downstream of p1:

  p2_redirect: fires when the successor the cluster would publish at
               p2 differs from the one ITS OWN p1 STAGE REGISTERS
               HOLD. NOT "disagrees with uBTB p1": the p1 successor
               is the uBTB's OR the loop predictor's, whichever the
               p1 mux selected (fe_decisions.md 2.5, and the Loop
               predictor line in the Overview above). Naming the uBTB
               is wrong whenever the LP won the mux. The comparison
               is one quantity against the cluster's own staged view,
               never predictor against predictor (FE-4). Corrected
               session-070.
               Target selection at p2 by branch type:
                 return     -> RAS ras_pop_addr_p2
                 indirect   -> ITTAGE (final; FTB target on miss)
                 conditional -> TAGE direction + FTB target
                 direct     -> FTB target
               TAGE overrides FTB direction (conditional only).
               RAS and ITTAGE are type-gated, not in the
               TAGE/FTB override chain.
               The per-slot successor is chained from the highest
               slot down, and a slot after a taken slot raises no
               redirect (ftq_bpu_interfaces.md 6, BP-121 D5, D15).

  p3_redirect: fires when SC CHANGES THE SUCCESSOR the cluster
               published at p2 -- not whenever SC overrides the
               TAGE direction. An override that leaves the next
               fetch address unchanged fires nothing
               (fe_decisions.md 3.1, FE-4; SC Role above;
               sc_interfaces.md Consumer obligations). This read
               "fires when SC overrides TAGE direction from p2".
               Session-070.
               SC requires TAGE output as input; SC cannot finalize
               before TAGE. Target for p3_redirect comes from FTB
               (held from p2). Direction comes from SC.
               No predictor produces a new target at p3.

Note: uBTB does not generate a redirect. It provides or withholds an initial prediction only. The override chain starts at p2.

docs.title: Dual Prediction Mode
docs.text:
Configuration: static input dual_pred_en (1 = dual, 0 = single).

Mechanism: the two slots are the two BRANCH FIELDS of ONE 32-byte prediction block, br0 and br1, each located by its own pos within the block's 16 two-byte positions, counted from the block start. The FTB and uBTB store positions region-relative and convert at their own boundary (ftb_decisions.md 4.6). One lookup supplies both (fe_decisions.md 10, FE-10). They are not two next-PC slots and not two PC ranges.

A TAKEN BRANCH ENDS THE BLOCK. FE-11: a RAS-operating instruction, and any taken branch, terminates the block, so slot 1 is not reached when slot 0 is taken. An earlier revision said the slots allow "a taken branch in the middle of a bundle to also predict the branch at the predicted target", which describes a second prediction past a taken branch. That cannot happen.

dual_pred_en DOES NOT CHANGE THE STRUCTURE. The slots and the channels exist either way (fe_decisions.md 10). At dual_pred_en=0 only br0 is reported and only upd_ch[0] carries traffic; nothing is removed. An earlier revision read "One update channel: upd_ch[0] only", which reads as a structural difference. Corrected session-070.

THE p1 SLOTS ARE IN POSITION ORDER. The uBTB does not reorder its slots, so bp_cluster swaps a uBTB slot 1 that lies below slot 0 (fe_decisions.md FE-10, BP-121 D12).

When dual_pred_en=1:
  - Both br0 and br1 reported per block.
  - Both update channels carry traffic: upd_ch[0] and upd_ch[1].
  - Each channel handles both conditional and indirect resolution.

When dual_pred_en=0:
  - Only br0 reported.
  - Only upd_ch[0] carries traffic. upd_ch[1] still exists.

docs.title: History Module
docs.text: Centralized ownership of all branch history state. Owned by BPC, not rename/dispatch. No SRAM -- purely registered state.

docs.title: Registers
docs.text:
GHR (Global History Register):
  Width:  GHR_WIDTH = 256b circular buffer
  Pointer: ghist_ptr (GHIST_PTR_BITS = 8b), OWNED BY bp_history
  Update: speculative on each prediction. Write pred_taken into
          buffer at ghist_ptr position, one write per active
          prediction slot in priority order, stopping at the
          first taken slot (BP-121 D16).
  Restore: on redirect, bp_history restores its own pointer from
           the checkpoint the rollback INDEX names. No pointer
           value is supplied from outside. bp_history_decisions.md
           2 and 10, bp_history_interfaces.md Pointer Ownership.
           This read "driven externally" and "accept new ghist_ptr
           from external logic". Session-070.
           Since BP-121 the rollback also carries a correction:
           bp_history restores to the bundle's first bit, writes
           the corrected bits and rewrites the checkpoint
           (bp_history_decisions.md 3.5).
           Recompute all folded histories from buffer contents.

PHR (Path History Register):
  Width:  PHR_WIDTH = 32b circular buffer
  Pointer: phist_ptr (PHIST_PTR_BITS = 5b), OWNED BY bp_history
  Update: speculative on each prediction:
            PHR[phist_ptr] = pred_pc[2] ^ pred_pc[3]
          One write per active prediction slot in priority order.
          Bit selection (pc[2] ^ pc[3]) is subject to tuning.
  Restore: as ghist_ptr above -- bp_history restores from the
           checkpoint index, not from a supplied pointer value.
           Same policy as GHR.

PHR folding is deferred. bp_history.sv maintains phr_mem and exposes phr_buf, but PHR does not contribute to any fold in bp_folded_hist_t. All current folds are GHR-derived only. PHR contribution to index and tag hashing is TBD, tracked by bp_history_decisions.md HI2 and tage_interfaces.md TI1. It is NOT resolved: an earlier revision said "resolved at TAGE and ITTAGE implementation sessions", and both units are now Complete and green with the question still open under HI2. Corrected session-070. The same statement appears under Folded Histories below; this is the one question, not two.

docs.title: Folded Histories
docs.text:
All folded histories maintained incrementally inside this module. Consumers (TAGE, ITTAGE, SC) read folded outputs directly. Exposed via bp_folded_hist_t packed struct output port.

One set of three folds per tagged TAGE table (T1-T4):
  tage_t<N>_idx_fh  -- index fold, width = FH for T<N>
  tage_t<N>_tag_fh1 -- tag fold 1, width = FH1 for T<N>
  tage_t<N>_tag_fh2 -- tag fold 2, width = FH2 for T<N>

One set of three folds per ITTAGE table (IT1-IT5):
  it_t<N>_idx_fh    -- index fold, width = FH for IT<N>
  it_t<N>_tag_fh1   -- tag fold 1, width = FH1 for IT<N>
  it_t<N>_tag_fh2   -- tag fold 2, width = FH2 for IT<N>

One index fold per SC table with history (ST1-ST3):
  sc_t1_idx_fh  -- width = SC_TBL_HIST[1] = 4b
  sc_t2_idx_fh  -- width = SC_TBL_HIST[2] = 16b
  sc_t3_idx_fh  -- width = SC_TBL_HIST[3] = 64b

Incremental fold update rule for fold of width W, history H:
  bit_out  = ghr_mem[(ghist_ptr + H) % GHR_WIDTH]
  new_fold = (fold << 1) | new_bit ^ fold[W-1] ^ bit_out
  where new_bit is the incoming pred_taken.

On redirect: recompute all folds from circular buffer contents at the restored pointer position (combinational, G15).

PHR/GHR mixing for index and tag hashing is the same open question as the one under History Module above: HI2 and TI1. Not resolved at the TAGE and ITTAGE sessions, which have happened. Corrected session-070.

docs.title: Checkpoints
docs.text: One checkpoint slot per FTQ entry (FTQ_DEPTH = 64 slots). Each slot stores: ghist_ptr (8b) and phist_ptr (5b) only. Folded histories are NOT checkpointed -- recomputed on rollback. Implemented as register arrays indexed by FTQ_IDX_BITS. Checkpoint written with post-update pointer values.

docs.title: Update Policy
docs.text:
Update trigger: post-execute resolution. No wait for retire. Both update channels exist in either mode. At dual_pred_en=0 only upd_ch[0] carries traffic; upd_ch[1] is still there (Dual Prediction Mode above, fe_decisions.md 10). This read "Two update channels when dual_pred_en=1, one when dual_pred_en=0", a structural difference there is not. Session-070. Each channel carries both conditional and indirect branch resolution (they are one combined channel, not split by type).

RAS update: speculative at p2 (separate from main update channels). Checkpoint/restore: the RAS snapshot (tosr, tosw, bos) is written into the FTQ entry at prediction and restored from it on redirect. Pointer-only; the circular data is not cleared. A flush is a redirect (FE-14), so there is no separate flush protocol. The mechanism is ras_restore_val / ras_restore_snapshot, built in ras.sv and driven by tb_ras. Nothing here is deferred to rename/dispatch. ras_decisions.md 4.3 and 4.4 are the single source; do not restate or re-derive the protocol here.

Prediction phase pre-computes meta-data needed for updates and stores it alongside the prediction result. Update path reads this stored meta-data rather than recomputing on resolution.

docs.title: FTQ Entry Split
docs.text:
MOVED 2026-08-19. This section carried a copy of the FTQ entry layout. The sole prose home is now planning/arch/ftq_entry_formats.md; bp_structs_pkg.sv remains the reference declaration.

The FTQ entry is two structures in two SRAMs, both indexed by the FTQ entry index: bp_ftq_entry_t on the fast path, read every cycle, and bp_ftq_meta_t on the slow path, carried per prediction slot and read only at post-execute update. What the cluster contributes to each is ftq_bpu_interfaces.md sections 4, 4a, 7.1 and 7.2.

docs.text: Open items and TBDs for this document are tracked in PROJECT_STATUS.md -- BP Cluster Open TBDs section.

docs.title: Settled Implementation Details
docs.text:
Parameter values derived in bp_defines_pkg.sv:
  TAGE_MAX_AWIDTH    = $clog2(2048) = 11  (max table depth)
  TAGE_TBL_SEL_WIDTH = $clog2(5)   = 3   (5 tables T0-T4)
  TAGE_MAX_DWIDTH    = TAGE_TAG_BITS = 8  (tag is widest alloc field)

  SC_NUM_TABLES      = 5                  (ST0-ST4)
  FTQ_CONF_BITS      = 4                  (confidence placeholder)

SC table roles are prose, not parameters: ST0-ST3 hold the confidence counters and ST4 is the BrIMLI table. See sc_decisions.md 6.

SC index array (superseded session-056; sc_imli_idx split retired):
  sc_upd_idx [0:SC_NUM_TABLES-1][SC_MAX_IDX_WIDTH-1:0]
  sc_upd_ctr [0:SC_NUM_TABLES-1][SC_MAX_CTR_WIDTH-1:0]
  Uniform 5-entry arrays (ST0-ST4). The original BP-001 rationale
  (ST4 index width differs, cannot form a uniform array) no longer
  applies -- indices/counters are packed 2D arrays sized to the max
  width across tables (session-058), zero-extended per table as
  needed. See sc_decisions.md section 9, bp_structs_pkg.sv.

RAS snapshot bundled as bp_ras_snapshot_t sub-struct within bp_ftq_entry_t. Access pattern: entry.ras.tosr, .tosw, .bos. Pointer width: RAS_PTR_BITS = $clog2(16) = 4b each field. See planning/arch/ras_decisions.md section 4.

FTQ entry history checkpoint (BP-002):
  ghr_snapshot (256b) removed from bp_ftq_entry_t.
  Replaced with ghist_ptr (8b) and phist_ptr (5b).
  Folded histories recomputed on rollback, not stored per slot.
  Implemented in bp_structs_pkg.sv.

docs.title: Timing Methodology Gap
docs.text:
Verilator does not provide timing data. Stage notation in struct comments expresses intent to Claude Code but is not verified by any automated tool. Jeff reviews RTL directly for timing correctness. This is documented as a known methodology gap.

Timing intent for BP cluster structs uses the prediction pipeline
stages, not the decoder's P-stages:
  p0.comb = combinational in p0
  p1.clk  = registered at end of p1 (available start of p2)
  etc.

The decoder's P0/P1 and the prediction pipeline's p0/p1 are now distinguished by case alone. bp_structs_pkg.sv CARRIES NO s2 OR s3 LABEL: the conversion was applied and verified session-070 (ftq_bpu_interfaces.md section 10, PROJECT_STATUS.md). This read that the struct comments were not inspected and might still carry them. Session-072.

docs.title: Methodology Notes
docs.text:
This is the second case study for the AI-assisted co-design methodology
writeup. Complexity drivers vs. the decoder track:
  - Micro-architectural decisions were open (not spec-driven)
  - Interfaces not predetermined by any external spec
  - Multi-module consistency is a real challenge (7 predictor
    modules plus bp_history and the cluster top, all sharing
    bp_defines_pkg.sv and bp_structs_pkg.sv)
  - Timing budget spans 3 cycles with conditional redirect paths
Raw observations to be captured in docs/observations/ during BP work.
